name: {N} {X} that changed {Y}
description: Case-study listicle — N independent events, decisions, inventions, or moments that each rewrote the rules of {Y}. Each chapter follows a tight shape: what happened → what changed because of it → what we owe to it today. Pairs natively with the Listicle / Explainer format. Examples: '7 plane crashes that changed aviation', '5 court cases that changed free speech', '10 inventions that changed medicine'.
subjectLabel: Subject ({X}) + domain it changed ({Y}) — e.g. plane crashes / aviation
openingDevice: Open by naming the stakes of {Y} as it stood BEFORE these {N} {X} happened — the rules, assumptions, or limits that everyone took for granted. One or two crisp sentences. Then promise: each of the next {N} chapters is a single moment that broke that world open and rebuilt it. Tease the most shocking case briefly, then hand off: 'Here are {N} {X} that changed {Y}.'
bodyStructure: Chapter 1: The earliest or most foundational case in the list. Three beats: the event itself (vivid, concrete), the immediate aftermath, the rule that emerged. End with a one-line micro-payoff naming what {Y} could no longer ignore

Chapters 2-{lastButOne}: Each chapter is one independent case study with the same three-beat shape. Move chronologically OR by escalating stakes — but pick one and stay consistent. NO recurring characters between chapters; each case stands alone

Chapter {last}: The most recent or most resonant case. End the chapter slightly differently — instead of just 'the rule that emerged', gesture at the rule still being written. This becomes the natural lead-in to the closing
closingDevice: Close by taking one step back: {Y} is the sum of these {N} corrections, and probably {N+1} or more we haven't lived through yet. Honour the people, systems, or losses that paid for each lesson. Avoid moralizing — let the stakes carry the weight.
